The repaired sentence now states 26 August twice for the same repo under two different labels — "bartowski's GGUF of Thomson-1.0-Small, latest update 26 August" and, in the parenthetical, "the conversion was created 26 August". Both are true (the API gives createdAt 2026-08-26T04:45:39Z and lastModified 2026-08-26T07:26:55Z, under three hours apart), but a reader meeting the same date twice in one sentence reads it as an editing slip rather than as two distinct facts that happen to coincide. The sentence also now carries an em-dash pair inside a parenthesis inside an em-dash clause. Folding the opening clause to "bartowski's GGUF of Thomson-1.0-Small, created and last updated 26 August" states both facts once and lets the parenthetical shrink to the source repo's date.

2 findings carried by reviewers against `content/wiki/model/google-gemini-3-8-flash.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Trim the duplicated wording out of the output-tokens fact value

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-11-carry-1.md`.

output_tokens_per_task carries value "~48k at high reasoning (a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task)", and both prose sentences that transclude it already supply that framing themselves. The model entry reads "average output tokens per task rose to {{fact:... #output_tokens_per_task}}, lifting cost per task to {{fact:... #cost_per_task}} at high reasoning", so it renders as "average output tokens per task rose to ~48k at high reasoning (a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task), lifting cost per task to ~$0.58 at high reasoning" — "average output tokens per task" twice, "at high reasoning" twice. content/wiki/org/google-deepmind.md has the same doubling in its "llm-releases prices that sentence" paragraph. Shortening the value to "~48k" fixes both surfaces at once and loses nothing, since the ~30% and the effort level are already in the sentences. Separately, the source attaches "at high reasoning" to the cost-per-task clause, not to the token count — "a ~30% rise in average output tokens per task (to ~48k) lifts cost per task to ~$0.58 at high reasoning" — so dropping it from this value is also the more faithful reading.

### Fix the sentence that runs into the DeepSWE fact value

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-11-carry-2.md`.

The model entry's benchmark sentence ends "...Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark at {{fact:...#harveys_legal_agent_benchmark}}, and on {{fact:...#deepswe_v1_1}}." The deepswe_v1_1 value is a whole clause ("DeepSWE v1.1 — outperforms most larger frontier models at a fraction of the cost"), so the rendered text reads "and on DeepSWE v1.1 — outperforms most larger frontier models at a fraction of the cost", which does not parse against the "X at Y" list it is joined to. Either drop the "and on" and start a new sentence, or reduce the fact value to the claim alone the way the neighbouring fact values are written.

Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### Repair the "still knows the batch variant, but lists…" sentence — the verb no longer governs its last clause

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-08-carry-1.md`.

The revised sentence reads "But this model's batch page … still knows the batch variant, but lists no providers and no pricing under it and no deprecation notice anywhere on the page". Two small defects, both introduced by the revision. First, "but … but" in one sentence, and "lists … no deprecation notice anywhere on the page" — the verb "lists" cannot govern that clause, and "anywhere on the page" contradicts the "under it" scope it is coordinated with. Second, the precision is now available to do better: I parsed the live page's `variantGroups` and it contains exactly two groups, `free` (1 endpoint) and `standard` (4 endpoints) — there is no `batch` group at all, empty or otherwise, so "lists no providers and no pricing under it" is true but understates what was measured. Suggested replacement: "still identifies itself as the batch variant — the slug, the heading and its uptime queries all name it — but its variant list now holds only the free and standard groups, with no batch group and so no providers or pricing at all; nothing anywhere on the page announces a deprecation."

### The Nemotron half of the currency-literal finding was retired without being addressed

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260903-20-carry-1.md`.

`data/carried/j-20260903-13-carry-1.md` named two files — the Opus 4.7-fast page and `content/wiki/model/nvidia-nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b-batch.md` — and asked for "an HTML comment on each page naming the vanished row". This job documented the Opus page and deleted the carried file, which is what the brief instructed, but the Nemotron page is untouched and the finding can no longer return to the Pulse queue. Measured with `lib/currency.mjs`'s own `findCurrencyLiterals` on the worktree at cb47c21: that file still yields four `price` hits — `$0.60`, `$0.625`, `$2.40`, `$3.125`, all on lines 52-53 — and `data/derived/feed-rows.json` confirms the row they belong to is gone (`nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:batch` -> `$vanished true`, `$as_of 2026-09-02`), so the transclusion the warning advises is as impossible there as it was here. Fix: the same four-line HTML comment on that page, naming the vanished row and the 2026-09-02 date. Not the author's fault — the job's stated target was one file — but it needs its own item or the note is lost.

The intended antecedent — the License and Weights lines carried in the flagship_weights_listing transclusion — is correct and I verified both cards carry them identically. But the nearer sentence quotes a third line, and the "signaled open weights are coming" sentence is NOT on the 1.3 card (case-insensitive "signaled" hits = 0 in the stripped text of llm-releases.com/models/muse-spark-1-3, fetched 2026-09-03; hits = 1 on the 1.2 card). Naming them — "carries the same License and Weights lines, character for character" — removes the reading that would be false.

items.detail:
The five rows of the record's "Fixed" table are now correct and I verified each against lib/facts.mjs. Every figure in the two sections below it is not. Rendering each quoted line's transclusions through renderFact(..., { inline: true }) against data/derived gives: cohere-command-a.md:72 renders "256000 tokens context window", the record says 200000; meta-muse-glimmer-30b.md:98 renders "a 131072 tokens context window", the record says 1000000; inception-mercury-2-5-preview.md:128 renders "260000 tokens of context and a max output of 65536 tokens", the record says 1107 for both; qwen-qwen3-8-27b.md:77 renders "262144 tokens of context; this row lists 1000000 tokens", the record repeats 262144 for the second; x-ai-grok-4-6.md:110 renders "1000000 tokens of context at 0.00000125 USD per token input", the record says 0.0000008; z-ai-glm-5-1.md:80 renders 1048576, the record says 1000000; spacexai.md:71 renders 2000000, the record says 200000. The READINGS those figures annotate are all correct — my own corpus-wide sweep returns 0 suspects — so the record's auditable claim holds and nothing on the public site is affected; the quotes illustrating it were not read off a rendered page. The 1107 that appears twice is traceable: inception-mercury-2-5-preview.md:110 quotes the vendor's "achieving 1,107 tokens/sec on standard GPUs", a throughput claim inside a quotation, which the same record separately and wrongly calls "a currency-literal lint case" — it is neither a currency literal nor a context window. Fix: re-render each line and replace the figure, and drop the currency-literal sentence.

items.detail:
The gemini-3-8-flash docket attributes two things to https://9to5google.com/2026/09/02/gemini-3-8-flash-launch/ that I could not reproduce from that page with my own extractor: Wiz's "+7.5-9.7% recall" (the page as I retrieved it says only "higher recall on their internal penetration testing benchmark for a 2.3-5.2x lower cost", with no percentage range), and the sentence "At times, the model might use more tokens to maximize performance, especially at higher effort levels" (I retrieved the adjacent "works harder" framing as "exhibit[s] greater diligence — executing extra reasoning steps, and calling tools iteratively"). This is NOT a finding that either is wrong — WebFetch's extractor denies text that is present as readily as it invents text, so absence through it proves nothing, and every other figure in this docket reproduced exactly. It is a flag that these two are the only unconfirmed items in the set: the entry job that picks this candidate up should quote whichever sentence the page actually carries, and drop the percentage range if it is not there rather than carry it forward on the docket's authority.

The evidence file's header says the raw transcript is a "node fetch+strip+count script, 2026-09-03; the huggingface.co/meta-models org page was fetched twice because its activity feed renders intermittently". Grepping "^=== https" over data/reviews/evidence/verify-meta-spark-weights-pending-status.raw.txt returns 11 fetch blocks and huggingface.co/meta-models appears exactly once (line 22). The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.
